text.title: RACI AI Assisted Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules every AI-assisted RACI matrix MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: Every row's `accountable` is exactly one role id from the roster: not a list, not a comma-joined pair, not "TBD", "team" or "various", and never the AI agent or an automation. A row with zero or more than one A fails validation and the matrix cannot be published.

rationale.source: PMBOK Guide, responsibility assignment matrix (RACI): one Accountable per activity

rule.rationale: Two accountable roles on "Login Endpoint" means the security review is each one's assumption about the other. Zero means the PM. The single A is the entire point of the matrix; an AI that hedges by naming both leads has produced a document that reads as complete and functions as empty.

rule.statement: Every row has at least one `responsible` role, and every role id in R, A, C and I exists in the roster as of the artefact's `last_reviewed` date. On scaffold, a prior cycle's A is carried forward only if that role is still in the roster and the WBS leaf is still open; otherwise the cell is left empty for re-assignment. A role that left the roster leaves every row it touched flagged `orphaned` until reassigned, and an orphaned matrix cannot be published.

rationale.source: Widely established RACI practice; this methodology's procedure (scaffold and roster delta)

rule.rationale: The matrix rots at offboarding: the backend lead leaves, the roster is updated, the matrix still says `backend-lead` on eleven rows, and for four weeks nobody is accountable for auth. Checking every cell against the roster at each trigger is a mechanical test that catches this on the day it happens instead of at the incident.

rule.statement: There is exactly one row per open WBS leaf, keyed by `wbs_id` matching `^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*$` from the WBS spec. Rows for summary nodes (a parent with children) are forbidden; an open leaf without a row fails validation; rows whose leaf is closed are removed at the quarterly review, not earlier and not silently.

rationale.source: PMBOK Guide, WBS and responsibility assignment matrix linkage; wbs-creation (upstream methodology)

rule.rationale: A RACI row for "2. Backend" hides that 2.3 (rate limiting) has no owner because 2.1 and 2.2 do. Binding to leaves makes coverage a set comparison against the WBS instead of a reading exercise, and it is what lets the roster-delta refresh be a diff rather than a rewrite.

rule.statement: Every row carries at least one evidence anchor of the form `charter#<section>`, `wbs-dict#<wbs_id>` or `stakeholders#<row>` that justifies the A assignment. An A the model proposes without an anchor stays `status: proposed` and is routed to the PM (procedure step 2 gate); a matrix with any proposed row cannot be published.

rationale.source: This methodology's template rules and procedure step 2; anti-fabrication practice for AI-drafted artefacts

rule.rationale: A model given a WBS and a roster will produce a plausible A for every row, including the rows where the charter is silent, and plausible is the failure: the assignment looks decided and nobody remembers deciding it. The anchor is the one field a reviewer can check in ten seconds, and the `proposed` status is how the AI's guess stays a guess.

rule.statement: `header.trigger` is one of `kickoff`, `roster_delta`, `quarterly_review`. A roster delta (join, leave, role change) MUST produce a refreshed matrix before the departing person's last day or within the joiner's first week; the refresh diff lists rows changed, rows orphaned and rows reassigned with their new anchors.

rationale.source: This methodology's trigger definition (AGENTS.md); widely established onboarding and offboarding practice

rule.rationale: "Refresh when needed" refreshes never. The three named triggers are the three moments the matrix is wrong: at start it does not exist, at a roster change it names someone who is gone, at the quarter it names leaves that closed. Tying the deadline to the person's last day is what turns a departure notice into a reassignment instead of an orphan.

rule.statement: A role appears in at most one of R, A, C, I on the same row. `consulted` is two-way (asked before the deliverable is decided), `informed` is one-way (told after); a role that only needs the outcome goes in I, not C. The validator flags rows where the C list is longer than the R list for PM review.

rationale.source: PMBOK Guide, RACI definitions (consulted vs informed)

rule.rationale: The AI-drafted matrix's characteristic defect is everyone consulted on everything: a security lead in C on forty rows is a security lead who blocks forty deliverables or ignores forty notifications, and either way the C is fiction. A role in both A and C on one row means the model did not decide. The flag is what makes over-consultation visible before the roster learns to ignore the matrix.

rule.statement: On publish, every person holding an R or A role receives their rows through the team channel, and the publish record in `review_log` stores the channel, the date and the rows sent. An assignment nobody was told about is not an assignment; a publish without a notification record is rejected.

rationale.source: This methodology's procedure step 4; widely established practice in responsibility assignment

rule.rationale: A matrix committed to a repo is a file. A backend lead who learns from an incident review that they were accountable for rate limiting since March has a fair point, and the matrix loses its authority for every other row at that moment. The record is what makes "you were told, on this date, in this channel" a fact.

rule.statement: `header.last_reviewed` is within 90 days (checked by `scripts/staleness-check.py`). The quarterly review removes rows for closed leaves, re-validates every cell against the current roster, re-runs the exactly-one-A and anchor checks, bumps `version`, and appends a `review_log` entry with `reviewed_at`, rows removed, rows reassigned and rows still `proposed`. A stale matrix is refreshed before it is used for any new assignment.

rationale.source: This methodology's staleness script and AGENTS.md (RACI rots within 4 weeks of project start without a loop)

rule.rationale: A matrix is a photograph of a roster and a WBS that both changed last week. Ninety days is already generous; past it the matrix is more likely to name a departed person than the current one. The counts in the review entry are what tell the PM whether the loop is working or whether the same eleven rows have been `proposed` for two quarters.
